as_told.title: Larry Smalley on a NASA asymmetric capacitor patent

plain: NASA holds a patent for a barrel-shaped, lopsided capacitor, an electrical part that stores charge. Michels raises it because this is the kind of device Thomas Townsend Brown worked on, an inventor Michels profiles as a scientist who built flying saucers, so the patent would suggest NASA took Brown's idea of electric propulsion seriously. Michels tells this himself in three episodes, and the details shift. In one he dates the patent to 2003 and ties it to a man named Larry Smalley. In another he calls it a 2004 patent from NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center under a senior engineer named John Campbell, and adds a Guardian article. In a third he dates it to 2004 at Marshall and again links it to Smalley.
